title: Word order: who does what
goal: Put the subject, verb and object in the English order
intro: English has a fixed order: Subject → Verb → Object → Place → Time. Hindi puts the verb at the end (“I tea drink”), but in English the verb comes right after the subject. Changing the order can change the meaning or just sound wrong.

examples: I go to the gym every morning.
We met at the station yesterday.

rules.rule: Keep the verb and its object together. Don’t put a word between them.
examples: I like Indian food very much.

mistakes.wrong: I very much like Indian food.
mistakes.right: I like Indian food very much.

mistakes.why: Keep the verb and its object together.

mistakes.right: I will go to the office tomorrow.
mistakes.why: Place before time, and say “to the office”.
In English the subject comes first, then the verb, then the object.

ex.y: Keep the verb and object together: plays the guitar well.

ex.q: I like very much your idea.
ex.fixed: I like your idea very much.

ex.q: She cooks very well Chinese food.
ex.fixed: She cooks Chinese food very well.
ex.y: Keep the verb and its object together.

ex.q: I every day walk to work.
ex.fixed: I walk to work every day.
ex.y: Time words go at the end.

ex.a: We had lunch at a small cafe yesterday.

ex.q: Put this in English order: “I coffee every morning drink.”

talk: Tell the coach about your normal morning: what you do, where, and when. Use at least four sentences in the order subject, verb, object, place, time.
